title: U.S. House · South Carolina's 3rd District
area: South Carolina's 3rd Congressional District (Upstate/western South Carolina)

context.text: Incumbent Sheri Biggs (R)'s June 9, 2026 Republican primary was canceled and she advanced without appearing on the ballot.
Eunice Lehmacher won the Democratic primary on June 9, 2026 with 53.4% of the vote, defeating Ernest Mackins.

candidates.name: Sheri Biggs
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced without a primary after the Republican primary was canceled

summary.text: Sheri Biggs is the incumbent U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 3rd District, seeking re-election.

background.text: Born in Mississippi in 1970. Earned a bachelor's degree from the Carolina College of Biblical Studies and a Doctor of Nursing Practice from Samford University.
Worked as a nurse practitioner before entering Congress.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Border Security and Enforcement; Transportation and Maritime Security subcommittees), the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Energy; Research and Technology subcommittees), and the Committee on Foreign Affairs (2025-2026 assignments).

candidates.researchNotes: Biggs has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; no current-cycle campaign statements were located within the research budget. Key floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Eunice Lehmacher
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary (June 9, 2026) with 53.4% of the vote

summary.text: Eunice Lehmacher is a retired medical social worker and psychotherapist running as the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 3rd Congressional District.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Concordia University (1985) and a master's degree from the Catholic University of America (1996).
Worked as a medical social worker and psychotherapist for Oconee Memorial Hospital, Clemson University, and Hospice of the Foothills, and owned a private counseling practice in Seneca, SC.
Serves by gubernatorial appointment on the Anderson Oconee Pickens Mental Health Commission and on the Sustainability Advisory Committee for the City of Clemson.

priorities.text: Increasing access to healthcare, especially in rural areas: restoring funding for Medicaid and the ACA, lowering the Medicare eligibility age to 64, and increasing funding for NIH/NIMH health research.
priorities.quote: I want to restore funding for Medicaid and the ACA and increase access to Medicare (e.g. lower the eligibility age to 64).

priorities.text: Helping residents with high prices, including opposing funding for ICE and long-term detention of legal immigrants and increasing apprenticeship and job-training opportunities.
